rationale.usefulness: Local narration, voice conditioning and expression tags are useful for reviewed teaching clips, interactive dialogue experiments and video drafts. The report provides concrete dependency, pronunciation, chunk-boundary and cache-invalidation checks instead of assuming that a small download solves deployment.
rationale.impact: A compressed downloadable speech component with several backend choices is a meaningful speech-domain development. Its contribution is constrained by untested quality, documentation conflicts and significant commercial restrictions; no broader AI-development change is demonstrated.
rationale.novelty: Ternary-body packing, optional embedding and decoder variants, and expression-conditioned local speech offer meaningful technical differentiation. They do not imply every operation is one-bit or that the model has demonstrated universally faster or better synthesis.
rationale.maturity: Inspectable package metadata, code paths and detailed chunk behavior make experimentation possible. Conflicting voice/language documentation, beta expression behavior, substantial example first-audio delay and no listening or installation test leave material reliability limits.
rationale.openness: Code and downloadable model files enable local inspection and several deployment routes. Commercial registration, revenue/funding termination thresholds, attribution, training-use restrictions and an unobtained incorporated AUP substantially reduce the freedom conveyed by Apache code alone.

concerns: The model license and unavailable incorporated AUP are consequential deployment limitations, clearly disclosed.
Voice/language totals and weight-size descriptions vary across documents; the report does not falsely resolve them.
The first-audio example is configuration-specific and cannot validate low-latency conversation or CPU throughput.
